title: Barriers to Accessing Mental Health Care for Older Adults With and Without Migration Experience (Tasks 1.4 and 1.5 of the EU Project EQUICARES)
summary:
Background:
Across Europe, many people face difficulties when trying to access mental health care - especially vulnerable groups such as refugees and older adults. These barriers go beyond the mere availability of services. They also include the ability to recognize the need for help, to seek support, and to obtain care that is affordable, culturally appropriate, and provided in a safe and respectful manner.
Research Question:
The study examines how older adults with and without migration experience perceive their access to mental health services. In addition, individuals who hold a relevant role within the health and social care system are interviewed. The central question is:
Which obstacles hinder older adults from receiving appropriate support for mental health problems?
Methodology:
The study consists of questionnaires and interviews.
Older adults provide a one-time report of their experiences with accessing mental health support.
Individuals who hold a relevant role in the health care system take part in a one-time interview to discuss organisational or structural challenges.

All participants are surveyed only once. Participation is voluntary.
conditions: The study does not focus on a single clinical disorder. Instead, it investigates the health-related issue of barriers to accessing mental health care among older adults.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Quantitative Survey (Questionnaire) - Focus on Access Barriers
General Population (n ≥ 75)
- Has used, or attempted to use, psychological or psychiatric services within the past 12 months
- Does not belong to one of the target groups (see below)

Target Groups (n ≥ 75 per group; 2 groups)
- Has used, or attempted to use, psychological or psychiatric services within the past 12 months
Belongs to one of the local target population groups:
-> Older adults ≥ 65 years without migration background
-> Older adults ≥ 65 years with own migration experience (i.e., born abroad and migrated to Germany)

2. Qualitative Interviews (Meso-Level Stakeholders) – Focus on System-Level Barriers
- Holds a system-level role corresponding to the Quadruple Helix Model (e.g., policymakers, administrators, service providers)
- Has recently been involved in mental health, service provision, policy, or research

II. Work Package 1.5 (WP 1.5) – Micro-Level Factors
1. Structured Survey – Focus on Perceived Access
- Belongs to one of the local target population groups:
-> Older adults ≥ 65 years without migration background
-> Older adults ≥ 65 years with own migration experience (i.e., born abroad and migrated to Germany)
- Has used mental health services
- Demonstrates the ability to participate in the survey without showing signs of significant emotional distress at the time of consent, as assessed by study personnel

2. Reflective Diary / Experience Report – Focus on Care Trajectory
- Belongs to one of the local target population groups:
-> Older adults ≥ 65 years without migration background
-> Older adults ≥ 65 years with own migration experience (i.e., born abroad and migrated to Germany)
- Must have accessed/actively engaged with mental health services in past 12 months (e.g., community-based, outpatient, or inpatient)
- At least one previous episode of meaningful mental health service use (e.g., inpatient, day clinic, or outpatient treatment)
- Is emotionally and cognitively able to reflect on specific episodes of mental health service use; most suitable for individuals with prior experience in using mental health services (written or verbal)
Exclusion criteria:
There are no separate or specific exclusion criteria. Participants are excluded from the study if the inclusion criteria defined in the study protocol are not fully met (e.g., not meeting the minimum age requirement, absence of migration history in the relevant cohorts, or lack of capacity to provide informed consent).
